newsitem.title: PERU: US group for Peru's Camisea power plant splits.
newsitem.headline: US group for Peru's Camisea power plant splits.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said Thursday the U.S. group composed of International Generating Co (Intergen) and Community Energy Alternatives (CEA), negotiating a contract with Shell to buy gas from Peru's Camisea field, has split up.
"They have told us they are no longer going to stick together as a pair," Andrew Vickers, Shell spokesman for the Camisea project, said in an interview.
Both companies could still bid individually for the contract to develop a power plant and purchase and sell Camisea gas, Vickers added.
The consortium of Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil Corp, which is developing the huge Camisea reserves, was also willing to receive separate proposals from from any other companies, the spokesman said.
"We remain optimistic the power plant can proceed. This is just a change en route," Vickers said.
Shell, which is the operating partner of the consortium, hopes to make a decision on who will win the contract within six weeks, he added.
Shell last August selected Intergen and CEA to exclusively negotiate the contract.

The Intergen-CEA power consortium had been evaluating the construction of a single 600 megawatt (MW) generating plant, which would initially supply up to 300 MW into each of Peru's north-central and southern electricity distribution systems.
Shell and Mobil, who in May signed a 40-year contract with the Peruvian government to explore and exploit the Camisea field, estimate gas could be supplied to the power plant by the end of 1999.
